title: Mittag-Leffler and Artin-Rees bounds for the cohomology of F/I^nF
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ the image of $f^*\widetilde I\to f^*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], with $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0). Fix $p\ge0$, put $H=H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ and $M_n=H^p(X,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ for $n\ge1$ (sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology]; these are $A$-modules, $a\in A$ acting through the image of $a$ in $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$), let $\rho_n:H\to M_n$ be the $A$-linear map induced by the quotient map $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$, and for $k\ge n$ let $\tau_{k,n}:M_k\to M_n$ be the map induced by the quotient map $\mathcal F/\mathcal I^k\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ (so $\tau_{k,n}\circ\rho_k=\rho_n$). Then there is an integer $c\ge0$ such that (1) $\operatorname{Ker}(\rho_n)\subseteq I^{n-c}H$ for all $n\ge c$ (with $n\ge1$); and (2) $\operatorname{Im}(\tau_{k,n})=\operatorname{Im}(\rho_n)$ for all $n\ge1$ and all $k\ge n+c$. (In particular the inverse system $(M_n)_{n\ge1}$ is Mittag-Leffler [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system]: for every $n\ge1$ the images $\operatorname{Im}(\tau_{k,n})$, $k\ge n$, are the same for all $k\ge n+c$.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02OB (lemma-ML-cohomology-powers-ideal, line 5553), parts (1) and (3) (part (2), the Mittag-Leffler condition, is the parenthetical consequence of (3)); its proof (lines 5586-5645) uses Lemma 02OA (lemma-cohomology-powers-ideal-application, line 5452) parts (2) and (4) (the fact used from 'part (4)' is in fact part (3)) for H^p and H^{p+1}, which rests on Lemma 02O8 (lemma-cohomology-powers-ideal-times-F, line 5405: the graded module of the H^p(X, I^n F) is finite over the Rees algebra), Lemma 0897 (lemma-graded-finiteness) and Lemma 02O6 (lemma-proper-over-affine-cohomology-finite), plus the long exact sequences of 0 -> I^nF -> F -> F/I^nF -> 0. Stacks writes I^nF for Im(f^*(I^n)~ (x) F -> F); this equals (I O_X)^n F as used here, since the image of f^*(I^n)~ in O_X is (I O_X)^n (on an affine open Spec B of X both are I^nB). Tags verified in tags/tags: 02OB, 02OA, 02O8, 0897, 02O6.

proof.text: (Setup: the short exact sequences and the ladder of long exact sequences.) Put $\mathcal I^0\mathcal F=\mathcal F$. For $k\ge n\ge0$ one has $\mathcal I^k\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$: $\mathcal I^k=\mathcal I^{k-n}\mathcal I^n\subseteq\mathcal I^n$, so each generating local section $as$ ($a$ in $\mathcal I^k$) of $\mathcal I^k\mathcal F$ lies in $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ ([def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0)). For $n\ge1$ let $S_n$ be the short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal I^n\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F\to0$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules; for $k\ge n\ge1$ the inclusion $\mathcal I^k\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$, the identity of $\mathcal F$ and the quotient map $\mathcal F/\mathcal I^k\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ form a morphism of short exact sequences $S_k\to S_n$. The category $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is abelian with enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], $\Gamma(X,-)$ is left exact and additive, and $H^q(X,-)$ are its right derived functors [pqf-def-cohomology]. By [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] (2) each $S_n$ gives an exact sequence $H^p(X,\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\iota_n}H\xrightarrow{\rho_n}M_n\xrightarrow{\delta_n}H^{p+1}(X,\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\beta_n}H^{p+1}(X,\mathcal F)$, with $\iota_n,\beta_n$ induced by the inclusion $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ and $\rho_n$ by the quotient map. Write $\alpha_{k,n}:H^{p+1}(X,\mathcal I^k\mathcal F)\to H^{p+1}(X,\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ ($k\ge n\ge0$) for the map induced by the inclusion. By [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] (1) applied to the morphism $S_k\to S_n$, $\delta_n\circ\tau_{k,n}=\alpha_{k,n}\circ\delta_k$; by functoriality of $H^{p+1}(X,-)$, $\beta_k=\beta_n\circ\alpha_{k,n}$ and $\alpha_{k,n}=\alpha_{j,n}\circ\alpha_{k,j}$ for $k\ge j\ge n$, and $\beta_n=\alpha_{n,0}$.

proof.text: (The constant $c$.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-powers-ideal-application] to $A,I,f,\mathcal F$ (the same hypotheses and the same $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$) with $q=p$, obtaining $c_p\ge0$, and with $q=p+1$, obtaining $c_{p+1}\ge0$; there $M_n$ is $H^q(X,\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ and $\mu_{k,n}$ the map induced by the inclusion, so for $q=p$ one has $\mu_{n,0}=\iota_n$ and for $q=p+1$ one has $\mu_{k,n}=\alpha_{k,n}$, $\mu_{k,0}=\beta_k$. Put $c=\max(c_p,c_{p+1})$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OB, line 5587: 'Let c = max{c_p, c_{p+1}}, where c_p, c_{p+1} are the integers found in Lemma 02OA for H^p and H^{p+1}'

proof.text: (Part (1).) Let $n\ge c$, $n\ge1$. By exactness of the sequence of step 1 at $H$, $\operatorname{Ker}(\rho_n)=\operatorname{Im}(\iota_n)=\mu_{n,0}(H^p(X,\mathcal I^n\mathcal F))$ (degree $q=p$). Part (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-powers-ideal-application] for $q=p$, with its $n$ equal to $0$ and its $m$ equal to our $n$ (allowed: $0+n\ge c\ge c_p$; then $e=\max(0,c_p-0)=c_p$), gives $\operatorname{Im}(\iota_n)\subseteq I^{n-c_p}H$. Since $n-c_p\ge n-c\ge0$, $I^{n-c_p}\subseteq I^{n-c}$, hence $\operatorname{Ker}(\rho_n)\subseteq I^{n-c}H$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OB, lines 5590-5611 (part (1): the long exact sequence gives Ker(H^p(F) -> H^p(F/I^nF)) = Im(H^p(I^nF) -> H^p(F)), and Lemma 02OA part (2) bounds it)
Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OB, lines 5642-5644 (implicit: the image of H^p(F) is contained in that of H^p(F/I^{n+m}F) because the left vertical map of the diagram is the identity)

proof.text: (Part (2), the inclusion $\subseteq$: the diagram chase.) Let $n\ge1$, $k\ge n+c$ and $x\in M_k$. By exactness of the sequence of step 1 for $S_k$ at $H^{p+1}(X,\mathcal I^k\mathcal F)$, $\beta_k(\delta_k(x))=0$, i.e. $\delta_k(x)\in\operatorname{Ker}(\mu_{k,0})$ in degree $q=p+1$. Since $k\ge c\ge c_{p+1}$, part (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-powers-ideal-application] for $q=p+1$ gives $\operatorname{Ker}(\beta_k)=\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha_{k,k-c_{p+1}})$, so $\alpha_{k,k-c_{p+1}}(\delta_k(x))=0$. As $k-c_{p+1}\ge k-c\ge n$, $\alpha_{k,n}=\alpha_{k-c_{p+1},n}\circ\alpha_{k,k-c_{p+1}}$ (step 1), hence $\alpha_{k,n}(\delta_k(x))=0$. By step 1, $\delta_n(\tau_{k,n}(x))=\alpha_{k,n}(\delta_k(x))=0$, so by exactness of the sequence for $S_n$ at $M_n$, $\tau_{k,n}(x)\in\operatorname{Ker}(\delta_n)=\operatorname{Im}(\rho_n)$. Thus $\operatorname{Im}(\tau_{k,n})\subseteq\operatorname{Im}(\rho_n)$, and with step 4, $\operatorname{Im}(\tau_{k,n})=\operatorname{Im}(\rho_n)$ for all $n\ge1$, $k\ge n+c$. (Stacks cites Lemma 02OA part (4) for 'Ker(beta) = Ker(alpha)'; the fact used is part (3), here (b), as written.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OB, lines 5615-5645 (part (3): Ker(beta) = Ker(alpha) for m >= c, then the diagram chase; set k = n + m)

proof.text: (The parenthetical: Mittag-Leffler.) For $n\ge1$ and $k\ge n+c$, part (2) gives $\operatorname{Im}(\tau_{k,n})=\operatorname{Im}(\rho_n)$, which does not depend on $k$; this is the stated Mittag-Leffler property.
